entries.title: Judges 20:1
segments:
Dan; in the northern extremity of the land. 
 
  Beer-sheba; in the southern extremity. 
 
  Gilead; on the east side of Jordan. 
 
  Mizpeh; a place south-west of Gibeah, and near the border of Judah and Benjamin. 
 
The sins of others, especially when great and aggravated, may be condemned; but without divine grace men will not abhor and forsake their own.

entries.title: Judges 20:4
segments: Men should carefully inquire into the facts, and obtain full proof of guilt, before they undertake to punish.

entries.title: Judges 20:8
segments: When men, in reliance on their own wisdom and strength, determine what they will do without asking direction of God or seeking his blessing, they should not think it strange if he does not give them success.

entries.title: Judges 20:12
segments: Men who protect criminals and screen them from punishment, become partakers of their guilt, and often of their woes.

entries.title: Judges 20:17
segments: The race is not always to the swift, nor the battle to the strong.  Men are dependent on God, and numbers merely can never insure success.

entries.title: Judges 20:18
segments: Which of us shall go up first; they did not ask, as they should have done, whether they should go up.  This, in reliance on their own wisdom and strength, they had resolved to do, and they only asked who should go first.  The Lord told them, but did not by this insure their success.

entries.title: Judges 20:23
segments: Men may externally seek the Lord without forsaking their sins, and in righteous judgment he may suffer them to take a course which shall end in their ruin.

entries.title: Judges 20:25
segments: Destroyed--of the children of Israel--eighteen thousand; the Israelites had themselves been guilty of various crimes, and God saw fit thus to punish them before he used them as instruments of punishing Benjamin.

entries.title: Judges 20:28
segments: Phinehas--stood before it in those days; this shows that these transactions took place not long after the death of Joshua or the elders that outlived him.

Or shall I cease? this shows that they were now in some measure humbled, ready to commit themselves to the guidance and disposal of God, and thus were better prepared for success. 
 
  I will deliver them; not without their use of means, but by such means. 
 
A disposition to be governed in all things, not by our own will, but by the will of God, is a good preparation for sure, ultimate, and complete success.

entries.title: Judges 20:29
segments: The promise of divine aid, rightly understood, leads men not to neglect means, but diligently and perseveringly to use them.

entries.title: Judges 20:35
segments: However numerous or efficacious the means which men use, their success comes from God, and in the Bible is ascribed to him as really as if no means had been employed.

entries.title: Judges 20:45
segments: Rock of Rimmon; supposed to be a place north-east of Gibeah.

entries.title: Judges 20:46
segments: The wicked in this world are often the means of punishing themselves and one another; and this, in the future world, may continue to be the case for ever.

entries.title: Judges 20:47
segments: In the rock; in its fastnesses.
